subject: Post-demo: integration checklist + schema validation and retry playbook
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: integration checklist + schema validation and retry playbook

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick post-call recap and the suggested technical next steps so your engineers have something concrete to work from. We left the call confident VectorIQ can integrate Redwood’s inference APIs without significant architecture changes; below are the pragmatic items we recommend for a first pilot and the follow-up owners.

High-level objectives
- Get a production-ready pipeline for structured outputs (JSON) from our chat/generation endpoints.
- Ensure deterministic validation and safe fallbacks when decoding fails.
- Plug in embeddings + reranker for candidate ranking and high-precision retrieval.

Recommended integration checklist (pilot scope)
1) SDK setup (owner: Dev)
   - Use Redwood official SDK (node/python). We’ll send a minimal sample repo.
   - Install and enable auth via API key + optional mTLS for Dedicated/Private later.
2) Auth & routing (owner: Marcus/Neha)
   - Short-term: API keys scoped to project and environment.
   - Mid-term: KMS integration + token rotation (if you onboard Dedicated).
   - Routing: test with region=us-primary and a cost-fallback policy to model-smaller when capacity bumps.
3) Structured output & tool-calling (owner: Dev)
   - Provide a strict JSON schema for expected outputs (we suggest a single top-level object with a discriminant field).
   - Enforce constrained decoding + post-parse validation.
4) Embeddings & reranker (owner: Neha)
   - Offload candidate generation to embeddings index, then call Redwood reranker endpoint for final ordering.

Validation & retry-pattern proposal (core ask you raised)
- Accept only responses that parse to JSON and validate against your schema (reject otherwise).
- Retry policy:
  1) Re-issue request with deterministic decoding knobs (temperature=0, top_p reduced).
  2) If still invalid, call a smaller distilled model with the same schema prompt.
  3) As a last resort, return a structured error result with the failure reason and surfaced raw text for manual triage.

Attachments: I attached a short integration checklist and a sample schema (schema-examples.json) with the proposed discriminants/fields.

Next steps
- Dev: I’ll drop the sample repo and an initial SDK snippet by EOD today.
- Neha: can you share your compliance point-of-contact so we can draft a SOC2 evidence packet?
- Sarah: does next Wed (4/28) 10–11am PT work for a follow-up technical sync?

Thanks —

2) On retries: what kind of latency overhead should we expect for the two retry passes (deterministic + smaller model)? We’re trying to keep p95 sub-600ms for user-facing flows.
3) For embeddings + reranker, any recommendations for the vector dimension and batch sizes for initial load?

Subject: Re: Post-demo: integration checklist + schema validation and retry playbook

Hey Sarah — quick technical answers and a proposed pattern your Eng can implement during the pilot. TL;DR: three-layer validation + idempotent retry keys.

1) Required vs optional fields - We recommend a discriminant-based schema: top-level field "response_type" (e.g., "actionable_summary" | "no_match" | "needs_human"). For each response_type define a small set of strictly required fields; everything else can be optional. This lets your service accept partial responses when the discriminant is "no_match" and triggers alternative UX. Example in schema-examples.json.

2) Validation layers (fast, robust)
- Layer A — constrained decoding: add a one-line instruction to the model prompt to prefer JSON only, and apply token-level constraints where available (e.g., allowed start tokens for objects). This reduces malformed output but is not sufficient alone.
- Layer B — fast parse + schema check: parse with a forgiving JSON parser (recover common issues like trailing commas), then validate against AJV/JsonSchema. If validation passes, return.
- Layer C — differential sanity checks & reranker: run a lightweight consistency check (e.g., ensure ids exist in your DB or that lengths are within expected bounds) and optionally rerank multiple candidates via the reranker endpoint.

3) Retry / fallback pattern (idempotent, observable)
- Use an idempotency key per user request so retries don’t create duplicates.
- Attempt order:
  a) First pass: normal generation (latency target).
  b) If parse or schema validation fails: retry once with temperature=0, top_p=0.6, and explicit "return JSON" rubric.
  c) If still fails: fallback to a smaller model variant (cost-savvy) with same constrained prompt.
  d) If still fails: return structured failure token with error code and raw text blob.
- Latency: empirical numbers depend on model size and your infra. For hosted Redwood models we typically see: base pass ~120–300ms for conversational-size prompts; deterministic retry ~150–350ms; smaller-model fallback ~80–200ms. Two retries in the worst case could push p95 above 600ms for large prompts — recommend using async background correction for non-blocking UX or optimistic UI with progressive enhancement.

4) Embeddings / reranker tips
- Start with 1k–2k dim vectors if you plan heavy semantic granularity; for a pilot 512 dims is often a good tradeoff.
- Batch indexing in 1k–2k chunks. For reranking, send top-N (N=10–50 depending on read latency budget) then rerank.

Attachments in this thread: I uploaded schema-examples.json with the discriminant examples and a short script to run AJV validation locally.

If you want, I can paste the sample node/python snippet into the shared Drive before the sync.
